analyst.summary: Vedanta completed its long-planned demerger this year: aluminium, oil & gas, power and iron & steel are now separately listed companies (trading since 15 June 2026), and what remains in Vedanta Ltd is a leaner zinc-silver-copper business built around its roughly 63.4% stake in Hindustan Zinc, carrying far less debt than the old conglomerate. Hindustan Zinc itself just posted a record year - strong margins and its lowest-ever zinc production cost - so the core asset is genuinely performing well. But the concerns that dogged Vedanta before the split haven't gone away: the UK parent still draws large 'brand fee' payments from the Indian businesses to help service its own debt (a practice regulators have already once forced it to partly reverse), a tax authority has flagged the parent's overseas holding structure as designed mainly to avoid tax, a shareholder has taken the brand-fee issue to the Supreme Court, and a fatal boiler explosion at a group power plant in April 2026 has reopened questions about safety and governance discipline. Vedanta also keeps selling down its stake in Hindustan Zinc - its best asset - to raise cash, and the government is weighing a further stake sale too. We don't see current prices as compensating investors enough for this unresolved list of governance, tax and safety issues layered on top of normal metal-price cyclicality. We rate it Sell.
